title: 2019 AMC 8 Problem 15
statement: On a beach \(50\) people are wearing sunglasses and \(35\) people are wearing caps. Some people are wearing both sunglasses and caps. If one of the people wearing a cap is selected at random, the probability that this person is also wearing sunglasses is \(\dfrac{2}{5}.\) If instead, someone wearing sunglasses is selected at random, what is the probability that this person is also wearing a cap?

solutions.text:
If the probability is \(\dfrac{2}{5},\) that means \(\dfrac{2}{5}\) of the people wearing caps are also wearing sunglasses.

This means that \(35 \cdot \dfrac{2}{5} = 14\) people are wearing both caps and sunglasses.

The probability of a person wearing sunglasses also wearing a cap is \(\dfrac{14}{50} = \dfrac{7}{25}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Use the cap group to find the number wearing both
Then divide that same overlap by the number wearing sunglasses
